text: One shared HTTP MCP endpoint lists tools from a disk cache and starts an upstream only when a tool on it is called; at rest there are zero child processes.
provider: RouterCore/Pool/StdioUpstreamTransport.swift:117 Process() -> /usr/bin/env; RouterCore/Pool/ProcessResident.swift:54 Process() -> the server's own executable. The 'zero child processes at rest' half is a claim about this provider NOT running.

text: The tool cache is keyed on each server's command/args/env identity and tools are namespaced <server>__<tool>.
providerNote: cache identity and namespacing are computed in memory; the disk cache it is written to is REQ-013's filesystem-write, not a second effect.

text: The Mac shell navigates eight destinations — Activity, Servers, Skills, Discover, Inbox, Checks, Cleanup, Settings — via the sidebar and ⌘1–7 / ⌘,.
providerNote: sidebar navigation is in-process SwiftUI state.

text: The Servers board reflects live server states from ServerStateTracker (running, tripped, never used, held) without inventing a figure the tracker did not observe.
providerNote: ServerStateTracker reads state the router already holds; the socket that delivered it is REQ-012's.

text: When the tracker is stale or the router is not running, live counts go absent rather than displaying last-known figures as current.
providerNote: an honesty guardrail about what is displayed.

text: The phone queues; it never installs. No path from the phone or a notification can put a server on the Mac without explicit human review on the Mac.
providerNote: the guarantee is that NO install path exists from the phone -- a requirement that nothing is performed. Its provider census is deliberately empty, and that emptiness is the requirement holding rather than a vacuity.

text: Numbers the router does not observe are never displayed. There is no fabricated memory saving.
providerNote: an honesty guardrail about what is displayed.

text: The menu-bar popover shows a readout, attention rows, and an inbox band of oldest-first arrivals; a partial row carries no review affordance.
Disposing an inbox item immediately withdraws its notification banner; a multi-item banner carries Review only.
providerNote: notification withdrawal is a UNUserNotificationCenter call inside the app.

text: The phone exposes Discover, Triage, Queue, Library and Settings; Triage commit is a single-batch undoable enqueue.
providerNote: phone navigation and batch enqueue are in-process.

text: RouterCore manages live stdio children and HTTP upstreams with single-flight spawn and idle reaping.
provider: RouterCore/Pool/StdioUpstreamTransport.swift:117 and RouterCore/Pool/ProcessResident.swift:54 spawn the stdio children; HTTP upstreams go out through MCPRouterKit/Control/LiveControlAPIClient.swift URLSession. Single-flight and idle reaping are properties OF that spawning, so this requirement is vacuous exactly if the spawn is.

text: The control API is loopback-only, authenticated, and refuses to write command/args/env through PATCH.
provider: RouterCore/HTTP/LoopbackHTTPServer.swift NWListener pinned by requiredLocalEndpoint; RouterCore/Auth/CallbackListener.swift NWListener on the fixed OAuth callback port. The client half is MCPRouterCLI/Loopback.swift NWConnection to .ipv4(.loopback).

text: Mutations to servers.json use atomic staging and a lock so concurrent writers cannot clobber.
provider: RouterCore/Config/ConfigMutationLock.swift:132 flock(descriptor, LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) and :146 LOCK_UN; RouterCore/IO/FileSystem.swift:56 data.write(to:). The atomic-staging half is the write-then-rename in the same file.

text: Swift RouterCore matches the TypeScript reference on the parity corpus; the cutover target is 82 of 83 with fixture-registry-search a standing exclusion.
providerNote: the parity corpus is compared in process against recorded fixtures.

text: Mac Pairing sheet shows an 8-character Crockford code and QR; the phone can scan or type it.
providerNote: the code and QR are rendered; contacting the other device is REQ-016, which is separately contradicted.

text: A pairing exchange actually contacts the other device and stores a record only after that contact succeeds.
note: I5 measured neither side implements a transport; the phone stores a paired-Mac record for a Mac it never contacted.
providerNote: NO PROVIDER IN PRODUCTION SOURCE. No symbol under app/Sources opens a connection to a paired device: the pairing exchange is unimplemented (DEF-001). This requirement is already recorded `contradicted` on other grounds, and the empty census is the same finding reached from the effect side -- the guarantee 'stores a record only after contact succeeds' cannot be violated by a build that never contacts anything.

text: Every data surface ships the nine DESIGN.md §5 states with real copy on the unhappy paths.
providerNote: the nine states are a rendering claim.

text: Undo is the Mac contract for reversible acts; a named-consequence dialog is reserved for genuinely destructive ones and is never the default button.
providerNote: undo and the dialog are in-process; the write they wrap is REQ-013's.

text: A refused write is shown as the server's refusal. Success affordances are not shown for work that did not happen.
